action.title: ⚡ Action
action.description: One thing the bot does when this rule matches.

oneOf.title: 🗑 Moderate the message
oneOf.description: Marks the message as moderated. The bot must have the **Moderator or higher** role in the group to perform this action. It works only in rules for when a member posts.

oneOf.title: 👁 Set the member as observer
oneOf.description: Sets the member — the message's author, or the person who joined — to the observer role, so they can read the group but not write to it. The bot must have the **Admin or higher** role in the group to perform this action. _A message that triggered the rule stays in the group — add the 🗑 *Moderate the message* action next to this one if it should be removed too._

duration_minutes.title: Restore them to member after this many minutes
duration_minutes.description: 0 keeps them an observer until you change their role by hand. The maximum is 43200 minutes (30 days).

oneOf.title: 🚪 Kick the member
oneOf.description: Removes the member — the message's author, or the person who joined — from the group. The bot must have the **Owner** role in the group to perform this action. _With **Also delete every message** left off, a message that triggered the rule stays in the group — add the 🗑 Moderate the message action next to this one if it should be removed too. With it on, the member's messages are deleted, that one included, and adding 🗑 Moderate the message changes nothing: the bot drops it as already covered._

delete_all_messages.title: Also delete every message the member has ever sent in this group
delete_all_messages.description: Deletes the member's whole history in this group, the message that triggered the rule included. Left off, they leave and their messages stay.

condition.title: 🔎 If
condition.description: What the bot looks for: in the message, in the member who posted it or joined, or in the group.

oneOf.title: 💬 Message Contains Any of These Words
oneOf.description: Matches when the message contains any of the listed words or phrases. **Whole words only, never a substring** — the keyword `ass` does not match `classic`, `assume` or `embassy`, and `anal` does not match `analysis`. It still sees through capitalisation, leet-speak (`b@dw0rd`), Latin/Cyrillic look-alikes, styled and full-width letters (`𝓼𝓹𝓪𝓶`, `ｓｐａｍ`), upside-down text (`ɯɐds`), letters spaced out (`s.p.a.m`), flooded letters (`spaaaam`), `@mentions`, and English plurals and endings (`spam` also catches `spams`, `sex` also catches `sexy` and `sexual`). A phrase matches when its words come one after another, and a keyword of five letters or more also matches when written split or joined (`blowjob` ⇄ `blow job`). _Ready-to-use lists of profanity: [🔞 List of Dirty, Naughty, Obscene Words](https://github.com/LDNOOBW/List-of-Dirty-Naughty-Obscene-and-Otherwise-Bad-Words), [☕ Google Profanity Words](https://github.com/coffee-and-fun/google-profanity-words/tree/main/data), [💬 Comment Blocklist](https://github.com/splorp/wordpress-comment-blocklist)_

keywords.title: Words / Phrases
keywords.description: The words and phrases to look for, one per entry. Each is found as a whole word, however it is disguised.

oneOf.title: 💬 Message Exactly Matches Any of These Texts
oneOf.description: Matches when the whole message text is exactly one of the listed texts (leading and trailing spaces are ignored).

case_sensitive.title: Case sensitive
case_sensitive.description: Off, capital and small letters count as the same.

messages.title: Texts
messages.description: The texts to compare with the whole message, one per entry.

oneOf.title: 💬 Message Matches Any of These Regex Patterns
oneOf.description: Matches when the message matches any of the given regular expressions (Rust `regex` crate syntax — no lookaheads/lookbehinds/backreferences). Runs against the raw, unmodified message text — unlike `Message Contains Any of These Words`, it does **not** see through leet-speak, look-alike characters, or other obfuscation. Use it for structural patterns (e.g. "`\d{4,}`" for runs of 4+ digits, "` {5,}`" for 5+ consecutive spaces) rather than for words. _Build and test your patterns at [🧪 regex101](https://regex101.com/) — pick **Rust** in the flavor list on the left, so it behaves exactly like this bot._

patterns.title: Regex Patterns
patterns.description: Regex patterns in Rust `regex` syntax, one per entry, matched against the raw text.

oneOf.title: 💬 Message Contains Repeated Sequence
oneOf.description: Matches when some sequence of characters is repeated back-to-back at least the given number of times — e.g. `aaaaa`, `!!!!!`, `hahahahaha`, `buy now buy now buy now`. Sequences can be up to 50 characters long; letter case is ignored, and spaces, line breaks and emoji count as characters. Note that numbers like `1000000` and dots like `.....` count too.

min_repeats.title: Minimum Repeats in a Row
min_repeats.description: Matches if a sequence appears at least this many times in a row. For example, 5 catches `aaaaa` but not `aaaa`.

min_length.title: Minimum Sequence Length
min_length.description: Shortest sequence (in characters) that counts. 1 catches single repeated characters like `!!!!!`; raise it to ignore them — e.g. with 2 and Minimum Repeats 2, the doubled letter in `keep` is fine but `byebye` is not.

oneOf.title: 🔗 Message Contains a Link to Any of These Websites
oneOf.description: Matches when the message contains a link to one of the listed websites or domains (including obfuscated links like `spam [dot] com` or `hxxp://`). A link written without `http://` or `www.` is only recognised when it ends in one of the common domain endings (`.com`, `.ru`, `.io`, `.me`, `.chat`, `.xyz`, …), so `example.pizza` on its own is not seen as a link.

domains.title: Websites
domains.description: Websites or domains to match (e.g., `spam.com`). You can list an entire domain (e.g., `example.com` also matches `sub.example.com`) or only a specific subdomain (e.g., `sub.example.com` matches `sub.example.com` but not `example.com`). Do not include `http://` or `https://`, just type the domain name.

options.phrase: contains a link to a listed website

oneOf.title: 🔗 Message Contains a Link to a Website Outside This List
oneOf.description: Matches when the message contains a link to a website that is NOT in the list (including obfuscated links like `spam [dot] com` or `hxxp://`). A link written without `http://` or `www.` is only recognised when it ends in one of the common domain endings (`.com`, `.ru`, `.io`, `.me`, `.chat`, `.xyz`, …), so `example.pizza` on its own is not seen as a link. Leave the list empty to match ALL links.

domains.title: Websites
domains.description: Websites that do not trigger this condition (e.g., `simplex.chat`). You can list an entire domain (e.g., `example.com` covers `sub.example.com` and `example.com`) or only a specific subdomain (e.g., `sub.example.com` covers `sub.example.com` but not `example.com`). Do not include `http://` or `https://`, just type the domain name. Leave the list empty to match ALL links.

options.phrase: contains a link to a website outside the list

oneOf.title: 🔗 Message Contains a Link Outside Top 100 Websites
oneOf.description: Matches when the message contains a link to a website that is neither in the built-in list of the top 100 websites (**Google**, **GitHub**, **Wikipedia**, **YouTube**, **Reddit**, etc.) nor in your extra list (including obfuscated links like `spam [dot] com` or `hxxp://`). A link written without `http://` or `www.` is only recognised when it ends in one of the common domain endings (`.com`, `.ru`, `.io`, `.me`, `.chat`, `.xyz`, …), so `example.pizza` on its own is not seen as a link.

domains.title: Extra Websites Added to Top 100
domains.description: Websites treated as if they were in the top 100 list. Do not include `http://` or `https://`, just type the domain name.

options.phrase: contains a link outside the top 100 websites

oneOf.title: 📏 Message Is Empty or Blank
oneOf.description: Matches when the message consists only of whitespace, line breaks, or invisible/special characters. Messages with attachments are never considered as blank.

options.phrase: is empty or blank and carries no attachment

oneOf.title: 📏 Message Contains Invisible Characters
oneOf.description: Matches any message that contains even a single invisible or formatting character (e.g. zero-width spaces, Braille blank pattern, bidi overrides, variation selectors), even if the message also has regular text. Emoji that are joined into one (like 👨‍👩‍👧) do not count.

oneOf.title: 📎 Message Contains an Image
oneOf.description: Matches any message that carries a picture, with or without a caption. A caption sent with it is the message text.

oneOf.title: 📎 Message Contains a Video
oneOf.description: Matches any message that carries a video. A caption sent with it is the message text.

oneOf.title: 📎 Message Contains a Voice Message
oneOf.description: Matches any message that carries a voice recording.

oneOf.title: 📎 Message Contains a File
oneOf.description: Matches any message that carries a file attachment other than a picture, video or voice message — those have conditions of their own. A caption sent with it is the message text.

oneOf.title: 📏 Message Exceeds Max Characters
oneOf.description: Matches when the message is longer than the given number of characters.

max_characters.title: Max Characters
max_characters.description: Matches if the message has more than this number of characters. Spaces and line breaks count too.

oneOf.title: 📏 Message Exceeds Max Words
oneOf.description: Matches when the message has more than the given number of words.

max_words.title: Max Words
max_words.description: Matches if the message has more than this number of words (separated by spaces or line breaks).

oneOf.title: 📏 Message Exceeds Max Lines
oneOf.description: Matches when the message takes more than the given number of lines on screen — for example a message flooding the chat with line breaks.

max_lines.title: Max Lines
max_lines.description: Matches if the message takes more than this number of lines. See 'Characters per Line' below for how long lines are counted.

chars_per_line.title: Characters per Line (Screen Wrap)
chars_per_line.description: If not 0, every line longer than this number of characters counts as several lines, the way it wraps on a phone screen: with 40, a single line of 100 characters counts as 3 lines. With 0, only actual line breaks count. About 40 characters fit on one line on a mobile screen.

oneOf.title: 👤 Author Hits Message Rate Limit
oneOf.description: Matches when the author sends at least the given number of messages within the time window, this one included.

message_count.title: Number of Messages
message_count.description: Matches when the author's messages in the time window, this one included, reach this number.

time_window_minutes.title: Time Window (Minutes)
time_window_minutes.description: The time window in minutes over which the messages accumulate (maximum 60 minutes).

options.phrase: author sent at least {message_count} messages in {time_window_minutes} min

oneOf.title: 👤 Author Hits Character Rate Limit
oneOf.description: Matches when the author writes at least the given number of characters within the time window, counting this message. Characters are counted across all of the author's messages in the window, so ten 200-character messages and one 2000-character message both reach 2000. An attachment's caption counts as the message text. This is the limit that catches a wall of text, where **Author Hits Message Rate Limit** catches rapid-fire posting.

character_count.title: Number of Characters
character_count.description: Matches when the characters the author wrote in the time window, this message included, reach this number.

time_window_minutes.title: Time Window (Minutes)
time_window_minutes.description: The time window in minutes over which the characters accumulate (maximum 60 minutes).

options.phrase: author sent at least {character_count} characters in {time_window_minutes} min

oneOf.title: 👤 Author Hits Line Rate Limit
oneOf.description: Matches when the author's messages take at least the given number of lines within the time window, counting this message. Lines are counted across all of the author's messages in the window, so ten 5-line messages and one 50-line message both reach 50. Each message is counted when it arrives, with the wrap width set then, so changing the width only affects messages sent after the change. An attachment adds no lines of its own — only the text counts, which for an attachment is its caption. This is the limit that catches a chat flooded line by line, where **Message Exceeds Max Lines** only looks at one message at a time.

line_count.title: Number of Lines
line_count.description: Matches when the lines the author's messages took in the time window, this message included, reach this number.

time_window_minutes.title: Time Window (Minutes)
time_window_minutes.description: The time window in minutes over which the lines accumulate (maximum 60 minutes).

chars_per_line.title: Characters per Line (Screen Wrap)
chars_per_line.description: If not 0, every line longer than this number of characters counts as several lines, the way it wraps on a phone screen: with 40, a single line of 100 characters counts as 3 lines. With 0, only actual line breaks count. About 40 characters fit on one line on a mobile screen.

options.phrase: author sent at least {line_count} lines in {time_window_minutes} min

oneOf.title: 👤 Author Hits Moderation Rate Limit
oneOf.description: Matches when the given number of the author's messages have been moderated by the bot within the time window. The message being checked right now counts too when another rule moderates it, so the rule fires on the very message that reaches the threshold: with a threshold of 2, on their second moderated message. Until the window runs out, it also matches the author's next message even when nothing else would moderate it.

message_count.title: Number of Moderated Messages
message_count.description: Matches when the number of the author's messages moderated by the bot in the time window reaches this number. The message being checked counts toward it when another rule moderates it.

time_window_minutes.title: Time Window (Minutes)
time_window_minutes.description: The time window in minutes over which the moderated messages accumulate (maximum 60 minutes).

options.phrase: author had at least {message_count} messages moderated in {time_window_minutes} min

oneOf.title: 👤 Author Joined Recently
oneOf.description: Matches when the author joined the group less than the given number of minutes ago. On its own it moderates every message from newcomers; combine it with another condition inside **All of These Conditions Match (AND)** to only restrict what newcomers post, e.g. links. Only members who joined **after the bot** was added have a known join time — members who were already in the group before that never match.

time_window_minutes.title: Joined Less Than (Minutes) Ago
time_window_minutes.description: Matches if the author joined the group less than this many minutes before sending the message. For example, 60 matches members during their first hour in the group.

options.phrase: author joined less than {time_window_minutes} min ago

oneOf.title: 👤 Member's Name Contains Any of These Words
oneOf.description: Matches when the member's name — the display name or the full name of their SimpleX profile — contains any of the listed words or phrases. In a rule for when a member posts, it reads the name of the message's author; in a rule for when someone joins, the name of the person who joins. Words are found as in **Message Contains Any of These Words**: whole words only, never a substring, however they are disguised (capitals, leet-speak, look-alike letters, spaced-out or flooded letters).

keywords.title: Words / Phrases
keywords.description: The words and phrases to look for in the name, one per entry.

oneOf.title: 👤 Member's Name Contains a Link Outside This List
oneOf.description: Matches when the member's name — the display name or the full name of their SimpleX profile — holds a link to a website that is NOT in the list, obfuscated links like `spam [dot] com` included. In a rule for when a member posts, it reads the name of the message's author; in a rule for when someone joins, the name of the person who joins. Leave the list empty to match a name with ANY link.

domains.title: Websites
domains.description: Websites a name may link to (e.g., `simplex.chat`); a domain covers its subdomains. Leave the list empty to match any link.

options.phrase: name links to a website outside the list

oneOf.title: 👥 Group Hits Message Rate Limit
oneOf.description: Matches when the group receives at least the given number of messages within the time window, from all members together, this one included. Every member's messages count toward the same total, so it catches a raid by many accounts that each stay under **Author Hits Message Rate Limit**. Each message that reaches the limit matches, whoever sent it, until the window has room again. Edits do not count.

message_count.title: Number of Messages
message_count.description: Matches when the messages all members sent in the time window, this one included, reach this number.

time_window_minutes.title: Time Window (Minutes)
time_window_minutes.description: The time window in minutes over which the group's messages accumulate (maximum 60 minutes).

options.phrase: group received at least {message_count} messages in {time_window_minutes} min

oneOf.title: 👥 Group Hits Character Rate Limit
oneOf.description: Matches when the group's members write at least the given number of characters within the time window, all together, counting this message. Every member's characters count toward the same total. An attachment's caption counts as the message text. This is the group-wide counterpart of **Author Hits Character Rate Limit**, for walls of text split across several accounts.

character_count.title: Number of Characters
character_count.description: Matches when the characters all members wrote in the time window, this message included, reach this number.

time_window_minutes.title: Time Window (Minutes)
time_window_minutes.description: The time window in minutes over which the group's characters accumulate (maximum 60 minutes).

options.phrase: group received at least {character_count} characters in {time_window_minutes} min

oneOf.title: 👥 Group Hits Line Rate Limit
oneOf.description: Matches when the group's messages take at least the given number of lines within the time window, from all members together, counting this message. Every member's lines count toward the same total. Each message is counted when it arrives, with the wrap width set then, so changing the width only affects messages sent after the change. An attachment adds no lines of its own — only the text counts, which for an attachment is its caption. This is the group-wide counterpart of **Author Hits Line Rate Limit**.

line_count.title: Number of Lines
line_count.description: Matches when the lines all members' messages took in the time window, this message included, reach this number.

time_window_minutes.title: Time Window (Minutes)
time_window_minutes.description: The time window in minutes over which the group's lines accumulate (maximum 60 minutes).

chars_per_line.title: Characters per Line (Screen Wrap)
chars_per_line.description: If not 0, every line longer than this number of characters counts as several lines, the way it wraps on a phone screen: with 40, a single line of 100 characters counts as 3 lines. With 0, only actual line breaks count. About 40 characters fit on one line on a mobile screen.

options.phrase: group received at least {line_count} lines in {time_window_minutes} min

oneOf.title: 💬 Flagged by OpenAI Omni
oneOf.description:
Sends the text of each message this condition checks to OpenAI's Moderation API with **your own** API key, and matches when a category below crosses its trigger. For each category pick **Off** (ignored), **OpenAI decides** (OpenAI's own threshold — every category on it is exactly OpenAI's own verdict) or a minimum score in percent (higher is more lenient). Pictures are not sent, and a message without text is never checked. The text leaves SimpleX's end-to-end encryption and is processed by OpenAI. If OpenAI cannot be reached, the condition does not match.

**The risk is the key:** it travels in every editor link, and a leaked key can call paid models. **Before pasting one:** 1) create a [separate OpenAI project](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9186755-managing-projects-in-the-api-platform) for this bot; 2) create a **restricted** key in it that allows only Moderations; 3) keep that project on prepaid credits with auto-recharge off — a monthly budget only sends an alert, it does not stop spending.

Inside **All of These Conditions Match (AND)**, put this condition last: the others are checked first, and OpenAI is only asked when they all match.

api_key.title: OpenAI API Key
api_key.description: Your own OpenAI API key, restricted to Moderations (see ⓘ above). The bot asks OpenAI whether it works when you send the rules, and refuses to save them if it does not.

max_attempts.title: Attempts
max_attempts.description: How many times the bot calls OpenAI for one message before giving up and treating the message as not matching. 1 means no retry. Only failures that can pass are retried — OpenAI being down, a timeout, rate limiting — not a rejected key. The message waits while this runs, so keep it low.

retry_delay_seconds.title: Pause Between Attempts (Seconds)
retry_delay_seconds.description: How long the bot waits after a failed call before trying again. Not used when Attempts is 1.

oneOf.title: 💬 Flagged by OpenRouter Instruction
oneOf.description:
Sends the text of each message this condition checks, together with **your instruction** and, if you ask for them, the messages posted just before it, to a model of your choice through [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai) with **your own** OpenRouter API key, and matches when the model answers that the message is what the instruction describes. The model also says why in one sentence, and that sentence is what the moderation notification shows. Pictures are not sent, and a message without text is never checked. The text leaves SimpleX's end-to-end encryption and is processed by OpenRouter and the provider it routes the model to; the bot only lets OpenRouter pick providers that do not keep the text to train on. If OpenRouter cannot be reached or gives no clear answer, the condition does not match.

**Setting it up:** 1) sign up at [openrouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai); 2) buy credits on the [Credits page](https://openrouter.ai/settings/credits) — they are prepaid, so leave auto top-up off and load only what you are ready to spend; 3) on the [API Keys page](https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys) create a key for this bot alone and give it a **credit limit**: OpenRouter stops the key once it has spent that much; 4) paste the key below and pick a model. Every checked message is billed to your credits at that model's price — compare them in [OpenRouter's model list, cheapest first](https://openrouter.ai/models?supported_parameters=structured_outputs&order=pricing-low-to-high). When the credits or the key's limit run out, the condition simply stops matching.

The OpenAI and Anthropic models sit behind OpenRouter's own moderation: a message it flags as abusive never reaches the model, and this condition does not match it. If your instruction is about abuse, pick a Google, Mistral or Meta model, or use **Flagged by OpenAI Omni** instead.

Inside **All of These Conditions Match (AND)**, OpenRouter is only asked once the other conditions match.

api_key.title: OpenRouter API Key
api_key.description: Your own OpenRouter API key (`sk-or-…`), ideally one made for this bot with a credit limit (see ⓘ above). The bot asks the chosen model a tiny test question with it when you send the rules, and refuses to save them if that fails.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model that reads each message, by its OpenRouter name. Each one here answers in the strict yes/no format the bot needs. Prices differ a lot between them: see [OpenRouter's model list](https://openrouter.ai/models?supported_parameters=structured_outputs&order=pricing-low-to-high). The `openai/` and `anthropic/` models never see a message OpenRouter's own moderation flags.

instruction.title: Instruction
instruction.description: What to catch, written to the model: describe what should match and what should not, e.g. "Match advertising: crypto promotions, casinos, unsolicited offers. Do not match normal conversation or technical questions." The model answers yes or no for each message, plus a one-sentence reason. The instruction is sent with every message.

context_messages.title: Earlier Messages Sent as Context
context_messages.description: How many of the group's messages posted just before the checked one are sent along with it, so the model can tell a reply from a message on its own — "yes, DM me" reads differently after "who sells?". The model reads them but judges only the checked message. Each goes with its author's display name, and the checked message then goes with its author's name too. Messages the bot deleted are left out. The bot keeps earlier messages in memory only, for up to 24 hours, and only while this condition is saved, so right after you save it or after the bot restarts there are fewer or none. 0 sends the message alone. Each earlier message is billed with every checked message, and is one more member's text sent to OpenRouter.

max_attempts.title: Attempts
max_attempts.description: How many times the bot calls OpenRouter for one message before giving up and treating the message as not matching. 1 means no retry. Only failures that can pass are retried — OpenRouter or the model being down, a timeout, rate limiting — not a rejected key. The message waits while this runs, so keep it low.

retry_delay_seconds.title: Pause Between Attempts (Seconds)
retry_delay_seconds.description: How long the bot waits after a failed call before trying again. Not used when Attempts is 1.

oneOf.title: 🧩 All of These Conditions Match (AND)
oneOf.description: Matches only when **every** condition inside it matches. Use it to narrow a broad condition down, for example a listed word **and** an author who just joined. An empty list is not a valid condition — add at least one condition inside, or remove this one.

oneOf.title: 🔀 Any of These Conditions Match (OR)
oneOf.description: Matches when **at least one** condition inside it matches. Note that separate rules already work this way, so you only need this inside another condition — for example _(spam word **or** spam link) **and** a new author_.

oneOf.title: ✖️ This Condition Does Not Match (NOT)
oneOf.description: Matches when the condition inside it does **not** match. Careful with conditions that already contain a negation (`… Outside This List`, `… Outside Top 100 Websites`), because the result is a double negative that is hard to read. `Author Hits Moderation Rate Limit` cannot be used inside this one.

templates.title: 🌪 Silence senders while the group floods

rule.name: Silence senders while the group floods

on.on: When the rule triggers, I notify you and carry out its actions.
on.off: When the rule triggers, I don't notify you and carry out its actions.

off.on: When the rule triggers, I notify you and do nothing.
off.off: When the rule triggers, I don't notify you and do nothing.

name.title: Name
name.description: What you call this rule. It is how the rule shows in the list, and the bot names it in its notifications.

trigger.title: When
trigger.description: What makes the bot check this rule: someone sending a message, or someone joining the group.

options.empty: No rules yet. Nothing is moderated until you add one.
options.prompt: someone sends a message (or edits one)
options.incomplete: Pick a condition and at least one action — the bot takes no rule without them.

options.empty: No rules yet. Nobody is checked when they join.
options.prompt: someone joins the group as a member or an observer
options.incomplete: Pick at least one action — the bot takes no rule without one.

enabled.title: Actions
enabled.description: Whether the bot carries out the rule's actions when it matches. With actions off, the rule stays in the list with its settings and is still checked, so with *Notifications* on it tells you what it would have done — a way to try a rule out before it acts.

notify.title: Notifications
notify.description: Whether the bot messages you every time the rule matches: with what it did when its actions are on, with what it would have done when they are off. Off, it never tells you about this rule. With both this and *Actions* off, the rule is fully off.

actions.title: ⚡ Then
actions.description: Everything the bot does when this rule matches. Add one entry per action — for example *Moderate the message* **and** *Kick the member*. The bot performs them in a safe order (observer role, then moderation, then kick) whatever order they are listed in, and skips an action that another one already covers.
